text:
sam: Heads-up — after the RBAC tighten earlier today I'm seeing a small but consistent uptick in mTLS handshake failures from ap-south services to eu regional ingress. Error snippets show KMS decrypt denies and `certificate verify failed`. Anyone on call?

viv: saw it too, ~09:05 UTC spike. quick logs: 
`svc-client: handshake failed: verify_error: unable to get local issuer`
`keystore: kms.Decrypt error: AccessDeniedException principal=arn:aws:iam::111:role/keystore-ap-south`

jordan: I pulled rotator logs — rotator promoted cert alias `svc-eu:stable -> svc-eu:2026-03-21-1` at 08:58 UTC from eu. Dynamo alias entries propagated to eu but the ap-south cache still had old mapping for ~7m.

infra-bot: kube-probe report: 09:06-09:12 UTC inbound TLS failures increased from 0.2% -> 4.3% for svc-ingress-apac.

sam: That timing aligns with when the RBAC patch removed `role/keystore-ap-south` from the KMS key policy. If an ingress pod tries to unwrap with that role (or via an assumable intermediate role) it will get deny.

viv: Repro steps I used:
1) assume role keystore-ap-south
2) curl to keystore endpoint to request wrap token
3) call kms:Decrypt -> got AccessDenied

Command snippets:
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111:role/keystore-ap-south --role-session-name test
# then
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id alias/svc-eu
```

jordan: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- re-add keystore-ap-south principal to key policy (fast restore)
- force rotator to re-publish alias->cert mapping and invalidate regional caches (safer)
- enable temporary ingress fallback to eu-canary pool which still has old key mapping (network config change)

sre-oncall: Priority decision? We need to weigh blast radius vs recovery time. Can we re-sync rotator quickly?

jordan: Rotator supports a cross-region consistency check script. I can run it now but it needs a small window (2-4m) and a brief pause on cutovers.

sam: Run the rotator resync first. If not recovered in 10m, revert the RBAC change for that role.

infra-bot: resync started at 09:10 UTC (cmd: `./rotator resync --regions eu,ap-south --verify`)

audit-bot: emitting audit slice for keystore.kms.Decrypt between 09:00-09:20 UTC: events=[aevt-9001,aevt-9002,aevt-9003], principals observed=[arn:aws:iam::111:role/keystore-ap-south, arn:aws:iam::111:role/rotator-service], results=[AccessDenied, Success, Success]

viv: After resync, observed Decrypt success for assumed keystore-ap-south principal. Handshake error rate fell from 4.3% -> 0.5% over 5m.

sam: Good. Follow-ups we should land before any future RBAC sweep: list below — assign owners.
1) KMS policy inventory and cross-role matrix (owner: sec)
2) Rotator publish check: verify alias table parity across regions + fail-safe hold if parity mismatch (owner: jordan)
3) RBAC change checklist: include a canary traffic test to keystore endpoints + audit event watermark (owner: viv)
4) Ingress TLS hardening: enable strict_chain_validation flag and log cert alias + leaf fingerprint on verification failures (owner: infra)
5) Add a short-lived allowlist grace entry to KMS policy for role principal->`kms:Decrypt` when performing cross-region cert rollouts (owner: sec + infra)

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-1102 ("keystore RBAC rollouts: add canary, audit watermarks, and cross-region alias parity checks") assigned to [sec, jordan, viv, infra]. Compliance note: SOC2 auditors may flag >5m gaps in audit evidence for key access; include audit slice in post-incident doc.

jordan: I'll add a pre-cutover rotator check that runs `verify-alias-parity` and aborts if mismatched. Also adding a configurable `cache-invalidate` call to push new alias to regional caches.

viv: I'll update the RBAC runbook with a canary flow: 1) apply RBAC in staging, 2) run canary webhook that performs kms:Decrypt test using an assumed role, 3) check ingress handshake metrics for 5m, 4) proceed to prod.

infra-bot: Infra PR queued: #infra/789 - adds `strict_chain_validation` default=true for internal ingress, emits handshake_fingerprint in logs. CI checks: unit + e2e TLS probe.

sam: Also dev note: we observed some older clients negotiating TLS1.2 and failing chain checks. For internal-only paths we should prefer TLS1.3-only but keep a brief compatibility window and an explicit whitelist for legacy clients.

sre-oncall: We'll monitor for 2 hours. If handshake error rate >1% for 10m, reopen incident.

audit-bot: Post-incident audit bundle: https://audits.example/SEC-1102/bundle (includes aevt-9001..9003, rotator logs, resync command output)

sam: Thanks all. Closing thread; will follow-up on SEC-1102 tickets.

sec-bot: auto-note: incident marked resolved at 09:24 UTC, follow-ups tracked in SEC-1102."
